key_insight: A locality-preserving fermion-to-qubit encoding (DK mapping) can keep 2D interacting fermion terms local while a constraint-aware HVA+VQE recovers low-energy physics and symmetry sectors efficiently.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more scalable variational simulation path for higher-dimensional Hubbard-type models by reducing long Pauli strings at the cost of extra qubits and physical-sector constraints.
method: Use the Derby-Klassen mapping to preserve locality in 2D t-V and Fermi-Hubbard Hamiltonians.
Enforce the enlarged Hilbert-space constraints through Clifford-based physical-state preparation inside a Hamiltonian Variational Ansatz.
Benchmark VQE performance against Jordan-Wigner circuits, including nonzero chemical potential and spinful Hubbard cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the DK-HVA accurately reproduces low-energy properties, resolves distinct symmetry sectors and degenerate states, and outperforms JW-style circuits when particle-hole symmetry is absent.
watch_item: The locality gain comes with auxiliary-qubit overhead and additional stabilizer/constraint preparation that must be implemented correctly to stay in the physical subspace.
paper_title: Investigating Interacting Fermionic Models with Locality-Preserving Qubit Encodings
